courses.common_course_problem_statement: Engineers struggle to investigate and resolve production incidents systematically.

problem_statement.title: Production backend service begins failing under load
problem_statement.description: A production backend service fails under load and engineers must identify root causes using logs, debugging tools and structured investigation. Complete 6 progressive artifacts to resolve this incident using a professional observability workflow.

problem_artifacts.title: System Failure Investigation Report
problem_artifacts.prompt: Production API latency increases during peak traffic. Create a first-pass incident map and list root-cause hypotheses.

problem_artifacts.title: Structured Logging Plan
problem_artifacts.prompt: System failures lack traceability. Design a structured logging schema with severity levels and correlation IDs.

problem_artifacts.title: Debugging Trace & Root Cause
problem_artifacts.prompt: Backend bug crashes services. Produce a debug trace and identify the root cause.

problem_artifacts.title: Bug Reproduction Plan
problem_artifacts.prompt: Intermittent production bug cannot be replicated. Create a controlled reproduction plan.

problem_artifacts.title: Root Cause Analysis Document
problem_artifacts.prompt: Engineers fix symptoms rather than root cause. Produce an evidence-based RCA document.

problem_artifacts.title: Incident Resolution Capstone
problem_artifacts.prompt: Investigate, diagnose, and resolve a realistic backend production incident using a full observability workflow.

modules.title: System Failure Investigation
modules.description: Learn how to investigate and debug system failures in production environments.
modules.module_specific_problem_statement: Production API latency increases during peak traffic.
modules.pressure_points: Engineers rely on print statements and cannot locate failure source.
modules.student_confusion: How backend systems fail under load.

learning_content.major_concepts: System architecture, request lifecycle, observability overview

support.module_continuity_link: Output becomes input baseline for Module 2 structured logging.

facilitator.question: Looking at the Final Incident Investigation Report requirements, what section do you think will be hardest to complete well, and what makes it challenging?
facilitator.follow_up: Agreed - that section trips up a lot of engineers. What is your strategy to tackle it?

facilitator.question: You just watched the Incident Kickoff video. In your own words, what was the primary symptom of the API latency spike, and what made it hard to diagnose at first?
facilitator.follow_up: Interesting take. How do you think the on-call engineer should have prioritised their first 15 minutes of investigation?

facilitator.question: What signals from the video would you look for first if you were the engineer on call during that incident?
facilitator.follow_up: Good thinking. Would those signals alone be enough to identify the root cause, or would you need more data?

facilitator.question: After reviewing the Failure Investigation Worksheet, what do you think is the most important column to fill in first, and why?
facilitator.follow_up: Nice reasoning. How would you handle a situation where you don't have enough data to fill that column?

facilitator.question: Reflecting on everything you have done in this module: what is one mental model or habit you would do differently in your next real incident, and why?
facilitator.follow_up: That is a meaningful reflection. How would you share that learning with a teammate who was not on this incident?

facilitator.question: You have just reviewed the System Architecture Overview slides. What part of the architecture surprised you most, and how does it affect the way you would approach debugging a failure in it?
facilitator.follow_up: That is a thoughtful observation. How would you document that insight so that a new team member could benefit from it?

facilitator.question: Based on the slides, where in the system would you instrument logging first if you had to pick just one layer - and what would you capture there?
facilitator.follow_up: Good choice. What would you sacrifice by instrumenting only that layer, and how would you compensate?

facilitator.question: The Request Lifecycle Deep Dive covered many hops. Identify the single hop where you believe latency is most likely to accumulate silently, and explain why.
facilitator.follow_up: Strong reasoning. What metric would you define to detect latency accumulating at that hop before it becomes a user-visible incident?

facilitator.question: The Structured Log Analysis Guide covers several log fields. Which field do you think gives the most diagnostic value during an incident, and what's your reasoning?
facilitator.follow_up: Good point. How does that field help you narrow down from hundreds of log lines to the ones that actually matter?

facilitator.question: Looking at the Service Architecture Diagram, which service boundary do you think is the most likely source of latency under high load, and why?
facilitator.follow_up: Solid analysis. What observability would you add at that boundary to catch issues earlier?

content.title: Reading Trace IDs in Distributed Systems

facilitator.question: After watching the Trace IDs video, explain in your own words how a trace ID flows through a distributed system and why it matters for debugging.
facilitator.follow_up: Great explanation. Can you think of a scenario where trace IDs alone would not be enough to diagnose a problem?

facilitator.question: You have started drafting your logging schema. What is one design decision you are least confident about, and what tradeoffs are you weighing?
facilitator.follow_up: That is exactly the kind of thinking senior engineers do. What would help you make that decision with more confidence?

questions.title: Failure Investigation Map
questions.description: Create a first-pass incident map showing service boundaries and symptom points.
questions.instructions: 1) Read incident context. 2) Draw request flow. 3) Mark weak signals.

questions.title: Hypothesis List
questions.description: List at least 3 root-cause hypotheses based on your investigation map.
questions.instructions: 1) Review your map. 2) List hypotheses. 3) Rank by likelihood.

questions.title: Evidence Mapping Spreadsheet
questions.description: Download the Excel template and map log/trace evidence to each root-cause hypothesis.
questions.instructions: 1) Download evidence-mapping-template.xlsx. 2) Fill in log entries. 3) Map to hypotheses. 4) Upload completed file.

questions.title: Root Cause Analysis Code
questions.description: Write Python code to analyze the log patterns and identify the root cause.
questions.instructions: 1) Use the provided log data. 2) Write analysis script. 3) Submit your code.

questions.title: GitHub Repository Link
questions.description: Create a GitHub repository with your complete investigation.
questions.instructions: 1) Create GitHub repo. 2) Push all files. 3) Submit repository URL.

modules.title: Structured Logging
modules.description: Learn how to produce high-signal logs for faster incident diagnosis.
modules.module_specific_problem_statement: System failures lack traceability due to poor logging.

support.module_continuity_link: Log report guides debugger inspection in Module 3.

questions.title: Log Schema Draft
questions.description: Design a structured log schema for a backend service with appropriate fields and severity levels.
questions.instructions: 1) Identify key log fields. 2) Define severity levels. 3) Add correlation ID strategy.

questions.title: Log Level Mapping
questions.description: Map common application events to appropriate log levels (DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR, FATAL).
questions.instructions: 1) List 10 application events. 2) Assign log levels. 3) Justify each choice.

questions.title: Structured Logging Implementation
questions.description: Implement structured logging in a Python service using the provided starter code.
questions.instructions: 1) Download starter code. 2) Add structured logging. 3) Include correlation IDs. 4) Submit your code.

questions.title: Log Analysis Report
questions.description: Analyze the provided log samples and write a report identifying patterns and anomalies.
questions.instructions: 1) Review log samples. 2) Identify patterns. 3) Document anomalies. 4) Submit your report.

questions.title: GitHub Repository
questions.description: Push your logging implementation to a GitHub repository.
questions.instructions: 1) Create repo. 2) Push implementation. 3) Submit URL.

modules.title: Debugging Tools
modules.description: Use breakpoints and runtime inspection to isolate backend failures.
modules.module_specific_problem_statement: Backend bug crashes services in production.

support.module_continuity_link: Debug trace identifies conditions to reproduce in Module 4.

questions.title: Breakpoint Strategy
questions.description: Plan a breakpoint strategy for debugging the provided failing service.
questions.instructions: 1) Review the service code. 2) Identify critical breakpoint locations. 3) Explain what you expect to observe at each.

questions.title: Stack Trace Analysis
questions.description: Analyze the provided stack trace and identify the root cause.
questions.instructions: 1) Read the stack trace. 2) Identify the failure point. 3) Describe the call chain leading to the error.

questions.title: Debug Session Recording
questions.description: Record a debug session walkthrough using VS Code debugger on the provided buggy service.
questions.instructions: 1) Set up the debugger. 2) Step through the failure. 3) Document findings. 4) Submit your report.

questions.title: Fixed Code Submission
questions.description: Submit the fixed version of the buggy service with comments explaining each fix.
questions.instructions: 1) Fix the identified bugs. 2) Add inline comments. 3) Submit your code.

questions.title: GitHub Repository
questions.description: Push your fixed code and debug notes to a GitHub repository.
questions.instructions: 1) Create repo. 2) Push fixed code. 3) Submit URL.

modules.title: Reproducing Bugs
modules.description: Create controlled test setups to reproduce intermittent production defects.
modules.module_specific_problem_statement: Intermittent production bug cannot be replicated.

support.module_continuity_link: Reproduction plan supplies validated failure conditions for Module 5 RCA.

questions.title: Reproduction Conditions
questions.description: List the exact conditions required to reproduce the intermittent bug described in the scenario.
questions.instructions: 1) Read the bug report. 2) Identify environmental factors. 3) List reproduction steps.

questions.title: Test Case Design
questions.description: Design a minimal test case that reliably triggers the bug.
questions.instructions: 1) Define inputs. 2) Define expected vs actual output. 3) Write pseudocode for the test.

questions.title: Reproduction Plan Document
questions.description: Write a formal reproduction plan document for the intermittent production bug.
questions.instructions: 1) Document environment setup. 2) List exact reproduction steps. 3) Define success criteria.

questions.title: Automated Test Suite
questions.description: Write automated tests that reliably reproduce and verify the fix for the bug.
questions.instructions: 1) Write test cases. 2) Ensure tests fail before fix. 3) Ensure tests pass after fix. 4) Submit code.

questions.title: GitHub Repository
questions.description: Push your reproduction tests and documentation to GitHub.
questions.instructions: 1) Create repo. 2) Push tests and docs. 3) Submit URL.

modules.title: Root Cause Analysis
modules.description: Separate symptom and cause to produce evidence-based corrective actions.
modules.module_specific_problem_statement: Engineers fix symptoms rather than root cause.

support.module_continuity_link: RCA report drives final resolution and validation in Module 6.

questions.title: 5 Whys Analysis
questions.description: Apply the 5 Whys technique to the provided production incident to identify the root cause.
questions.instructions: 1) Start with the symptom. 2) Ask 'why' 5 times. 3) Document each answer.

questions.title: Fishbone Diagram
questions.description: Create a fishbone (Ishikawa) diagram mapping all contributing factors to the incident.
questions.instructions: 1) Identify the problem. 2) Map categories (People, Process, Technology). 3) List contributing factors.

questions.title: RCA Report
questions.description: Write a complete Root Cause Analysis report for the production incident using the provided template.
questions.instructions: 1) Download RCA template. 2) Fill in all sections. 3) Include evidence and timeline. 4) Upload completed report.

questions.title: Corrective Action Plan
questions.description: Define corrective and preventive actions to prevent recurrence.
questions.instructions: 1) List immediate fixes. 2) Define long-term preventive measures. 3) Assign owners and timelines.

questions.title: GitHub Repository
questions.description: Push your RCA documentation and any supporting code to GitHub.
questions.instructions: 1) Create repo. 2) Push all artifacts. 3) Submit URL.

questions.title: Observability Stack Design

questions.title: GitHub Repository
